newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end higher after Bundesbank boost.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end higher after Bundesbank boost.

text.p: MILAN, Aug 12 - Italian stocks closed higher on Tuesday after the Bundesbank set a repo tender at an unchanged fixed rate which settled worries over German interest rates and supported by the firmer trend in early Wall Street trading.
Dealers said that trading on the Milan bourse was generally cautious today ahead of Thursday's options expiry and Friday's public and market holiday.
All-share Mibtel index closed up 1.57 percent at 14,600 and the Mib30 blue chip index 1.92 percent firmer at 22,067, and the September Fib30 contract 1.51 percent higher at 22,160.

The financial sector moved back into the limelight with selective buying being seen. BCI was up 4.11 percent at 4,278 lire and Credito Italiano rose 2.46 percent to 3,495 lire. Giant insurer Generali gained 3.79 percent to 36,467 lire.
Dealers added that the market was set to remain largely neglected over the holiday period and only sporadic buying in specific stocks helped to keep some interest in the market.
Oil giant ENI ended 1.76 percent higher at 10,435 lire, Fiat was up 0.38 percent at 5,845, Olivetti 2.49 percent firmer at 645 and Pirelli increased 2.22 percent to 4,827 lire.
